accepted.sentence: When successive notes permit multiple slide locations, players may choose an alternate route that keeps a quick passage compact and avoids awkward reaches.
For rapid repeated notes, performers may double-tongue by alternating tongue syllables, producing more attacks than a single articulation allows.
A performer can flutter-tongue by rolling the tongue while blowing, adding a rattling texture to a sustained or repeated note.
To create vibrato, players sometimes move the slide slightly back and forth in a regular pulse while sustaining a pitch.
Lip-slur exercises connect neighboring resonant notes without moving the slide, developing control over changes in lip vibration and airflow.
With a plunger mute held near the bell, performers open and close the gap to shape a changing, speechlike tone.
Before playing, performers typically connect the slide and bell sections, then secure their threaded joint without forcing the parts together.
For periodic cleaning, players separate the sections and rinse the tubing with lukewarm water and mild soap, avoiding heat that could damage the finish.
